name: Long-generation token integrity v1
description: Runs all 36 items of eval-longgen-integrity-v1 at temperature 0, concurrency 1, with a 3000-token output budget, and reports the share of generations that came back with no spliced token. Each item hands the model a 20-25k-character synthetic JavaScript project and asks for one complete new module of 150 to 290 lines, so the measurement is what happens to a decode path over one to two thousand consecutive tokens. Concurrency 1 is part of the configuration under test, not a convenience: the failure this exists for was observed on a single sequence, and batching changes the scheduler, the KV-cache layout and the attention path it runs through. Pinned together with the dataset: a change to either means a new -v2 id.

eval.notes: accuracy here is the share of generations containing NO spliced token, not the share of correct programs. A model that writes wrong but well-formed code scores 1.0; a model that writes a perfect module with one `carrierhed` in it scores 0 for that item. The scorer masks strings, comments and regex literals, then reports only five shapes: a digit-initial token that is not a valid numeric literal (`128Pin`), an undefined identifier that is a defined name — down to a single letter — plus 2-6 lower-case letters (`carrierhed`, `zhed`), a property name welded from a property the file itself defines (`ship.bobAmporton` with `bobAmp:` in the file), an undefined bare word or dotted fragment between two numeric literals in a comma-separated list (`[6, visible, 0]`, `[2, 0, .src, 4]`), and any non-ASCII character in code (`[2, 0, 惯, 4]`). A welded name that recurs counts once per generation. Ordinary undefined identifiers are not counted. Calibrated against the engine's own logprobs on 48 generations of the motivating build: the scorer finds 53 and 47 splices where the top-5 logprobs show 54 and 47 junk-argmax steps. A model that truncates before finishing the module still gets its partial output scored — a short generation is a weaker measurement, not a failed one — so read avg_output_tokens alongside the accuracy.

notes: accuracy and avg_latency_ms live in the result's `scores` block, not in `metrics`; success_rate is the share of requests that completed at all and is independent of whether the generations were intact. A clean run of 36 is NOT proof of absence. On the build that motivated this workload the observed rate was roughly one affected generation in five, and two clean runs of 24 preceded a run in which 7 of 24 came back spliced, so a single clean pass is consistent with an affected build. Report the run; do not report the absence. A model that thinks by default must have its thinking switched off in the packet's `request` block (`atlas-bench packet --request 'chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": false}'`, or whatever the engine's template expects): the 3000-token budget is the output budget, and a run that spends it on a thought block comes back with 36 items scored `no code in response` and an accuracy of 0.0 that says nothing about splices. The `reasoning: "default"` param deliberately leaves the engine's reasoning setting alone, so this is the packet's job, not the workload's. Two follow-ups are deliberately left out of this v1: the runner has no per-workload `extra_body`, so `return_token_ids` cannot be requested here without a harness change plus a retry-on-400 path for engines that reject unknown fields, and the result schema's `scores.avg_output_tokens` is not listed in metrics_required because kind=eval fixes that list at accuracy/success_rate/avg_latency_ms. Both are worth a v2 once the harness supports them; the runner already records avg_output_tokens in `scores`.
